answer: Dentate gyrus. Bad responders show the highest number of significantly differentially expressed genes (padj < 0.05, |log2FoldChange| > 0.5, baseMean > 10) compared to controls in the dentate gyrus: 245 genes (194 up, 51 down), versus 93 genes (88 up, 5 down) in baseline blood and 21 genes (15 up, 6 down) in final blood. The ranking is unchanged under the strictly-positive-lfc sensitivity check (dentate gyrus 194, baseline blood 88, final blood 15). Counts come from the precomputed DESeq2 bad_responder-vs-Control comparison blocks in the NormCount sheet (Comp2 = baseline blood, Comp5 = dentate gyrus, Comp8 = final blood; comparison identities verified by matching baseMeanA/baseMeanB to per-group means of the normalized counts); padj is the DESeq2 Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-value already stored in the file, and NA/inf padj values were treated as non-significant.
